_comment: The ONE place Growth Audit copy lives. The page imports this directly. The Apps Script gets it injected by scripts/sync-audit-copy.mjs, so the page and the email cannot disagree. After editing, run: npm run sync:audit-copy

verdicts.strong: Your funnel is in good shape. The gains left are specific, not structural.
verdicts.mixed: The foundations are there. One stage is holding the rest of the funnel back.
verdicts.weak: Growth is leaking in more than one place, and the stages are compounding on each other.

Acquisition.read: You are spending into channels without a clean read on which ones pay back. That is why adding budget has stopped adding growth.
Acquisition.cause: No one owns the channel portfolio, so channels get added and never retired. Blended CAC hides the losers inside the average.
Acquisition.move: Split CAC by channel for the last 90 days, then cut or cap the worst performer for one full cycle and watch what happens to pipeline.

Activation.read: New users are not reliably reaching value, so everything you spend on acquisition leaks straight back out.
Activation.cause: The activation moment is not defined in writing, so Product, Marketing, and Support are each optimising for a different finish line.
Activation.move: Write down the single action that marks a user as activated, then measure what share of signups hit it within their first week.

Conversion.read: Deals are turning on the individual rep and the individual conversation rather than on a story that holds up every time.
Conversion.cause: Positioning and messaging have no owner, so each rep rebuilds the pitch themselves and loss reasons never get written down.
Conversion.move: Write up the last five lost deals in one page. The repeated objection is your messaging gap, and it is usually fixable in a week.

Retention.read: Retention is being handled reactively. You find out about churn once it has already happened, and expansion is left on the table.
Retention.cause: Retention sits between Sales and CS, so no one is accountable for it and expansion revenue never gets a real number.
Retention.move: Give retention one named owner, then track expansion revenue as a hard number rather than an estimate for one quarter.
